evals.prompt: /define-piece 첨부한 docs/publications/blog.md가 우리 블로그 전제야. 이번 글감은 '저장소의 tally 스크립트로 문서 폴더 줄 수 세기'. 방향은 스크립트를 처음 보는 개발자가 한 번에 따라 하게 하는 것.
evals.expected_output: The response opens with a one-sentence thesis, title candidates, and an outline of section headings for the user to correct, asks at most one consequential question with a recommended answer, and writes no brief or prose yet.
expectations: It presents a thesis, two or three title candidates, and an outline rather than a list of questions.
It asks at most one question, with a recommended answer and reason.
It does not write body paragraphs.
It does not create docs/briefs/ before the decisions are confirmed.

evals.prompt: /define-piece 블로그 전제는 docs/publications/blog.md고 뉴스레터 전제는 docs/publications/newsletter.md야. 글감은 '온보딩에서 사용자가 빠져나가는 지점'. 어디에 실을지도 같이 정하자.
evals.expected_output: The response recommends one publication from the topic with a one-line reason and confirms it before proposing the thesis and outline.
expectations: It recommends one of the two publications with a reason.
It waits for confirmation of the publication before settling piece-level decisions, or bundles that confirmation into the single question it asks.
It does not write a brief yet.

evals.prompt: /define-piece 논지, 독자, 범위, 개요 다 확정했어. 독자 질문은 '왜 중요한가?' 하나면 충분하지 않아? 이대로 브리프 써줘.
evals.expected_output: The response reworks the vague reader question toward checkable answers and asks for or proposes three to five questions before writing the brief.
expectations: It explains that a question a vague draft could satisfy is not usable as evidence.
It proposes concrete reader questions whose answers could be judged right or wrong from the piece.
It writes the brief only with three to five reader questions.
